question: What is the meaning of renewable energy in relation to circular production?
description: Renewable energy is a key component of circular production as it enables the transition from fossil fuels to cleaner, more sustainable sources of energy. In the context of circular economy, renewable energy supports the regeneration of natural capital and the reduction of waste and pollution, aligning with the principles of circular economy. By integrating renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, into circular production systems, it is possible to minimize the environmental impact of production processes and promote the long-term sustainability of products and materials. This approach is particularly relevant in the built environment, where the construction and operation of buildings account for a significant portion of global resource consumption and waste generation. By adopting renewable energy sources, circular production systems can reduce greenhouse gas emissions, conserve natural resources, and promote the longevity of products and materials, thereby contributing to a more sustainable and regenerative economy.

The circular economy is a system that enables resource efficiency by 
minimizing waste and maximizing the reuse and recycling of materials 
(Ellen MacArthur, 2013). It aims to eradicate waste and pollution, and 
support the longevity of products and materials, thereby preserving, 
restoring, and regenerating natural capital (Sch¨oggl et al., 2023). In the 
built environment, where the construction and operation of buildings 
account for a significant portion of global resource consumption and 
waste generation, transformation to the circular economy offers a 
promising solution to promote sustainable production and consumption 
as well as reduce the resulting environmental and societal impact 
(Calzolari et al., 2021). Circular economy, as depicted in Fig. 1, includes 
components such as circular business model (Ranta et al., 2018), circular
